script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Comedy
Theme: small-town life

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. COUNTRY CAFE - DAY

A small, quaint cafe nestled in the heart of the picturesque village of Sunflowers. The sweet scent of freshly baked pastries wafts through the open window, drawing in customers.

Waitress LUCY (mid 30s, cheerful and friendly) takes orders from regular customers as they laugh and chat.

INT. COUNTRY CAFE - KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS

LUCY bakes fresh scones, humming along to the radio. The door swings open, revealing SALLY (early 20s, clumsy and anxious), a new waitress, carrying a tray of dirty dishes.

SALLY
(nervously)
Lucy, I'm so sorry, I dropped these.

LUCY
(laughs)
No worries, Sally. It's all part of the job.

INT. COUNTRY CAFE - DINING ROOM - LATER

Customers continue to come and go, all greeted warmly by Lucy and Sally. A local farmer, HAROLD (late 50s, gruff but kind-hearted), enters, and the two women exchange pleasantries.

INT. COUNTRY CAFE - AFTERNOON

Sally nervously approaches Lucy, looking worried.

SALLY
(whispers)
I know I've only been working here a week, but I can't seem to get the hang of this. I'm afraid I'll make a mistake and embarrass myself.

LUCY
(smiling)
Don't worry, Sally. We all make mistakes. That's how we learn.

INT. COUNTRY CAFE - EVENING

The cafe begins to empty, and Lucy and Sally tidy up. As they wash the dishes, they chat about their lives and dreams.

SALLY
(sighs)
I've always wanted to be a chef, but I don't have the money for culinary school.

LUCY
Well, you're a quick learner, Sally. Who knows, maybe one day you'll be the one baking scones for us.

INT. COUNTRY CAFE - NIGHT

The cafe is closed, and Lucy and Sally count the day's earnings. They share a laugh as they realize they've made a mistake and counted the same money twice.

INT. VILLAGE SQUARE - DAY

The sun rises over the village, and the women gather for the weekly market. Harold approaches, offering a basket of fresh fruits and vegetables.

HAROLD
I thought you ladies might want some fresh produce for your cafe.

LUCY
(grateful)
Thank you, Harold. We appreciate it.

INT. COUNTRY CAFE - DAY

As the cafe fills with customers once more, Lucy and Sally work together smoothly, their friendship growing stronger by the day.

INT. COUNTRY CAFE - EVENING

The sun sets, and the cafe begins to close. Lucy and Sally tidy up, sharing stories about their lives and dreams for the future.

FADE OUT.

THE END
